sessions.title: Welcome to Pioneer
sessions.must: Board, launch, keep an Earth object, glimpse an anomaly and end on the route log.

sessions.title: The Pioneer
sessions.must: Resolve the maintenance incident and reveal the repair record from tomorrow.

sessions.title: The First Anomaly
sessions.must: Connect four anomalies, hear Iris say ‘Both,’ and end on the sealed +103 DAYS packet.

venn.name: Captain Mara Venn
venn.opening: Cohort 01, you were selected because this mission requires people who can adapt for decades, not simply survive a launch. Asteria is not a rescue. It is a beginning.

replies.question: Why leave a healthy Earth?
replies.text: Because humanity should never have only one home. Earth is not dying. We are choosing to build a second civilization on Asteria-4.

replies.question: What do you need from the crew?
replies.text: We will disagree. When we do, speak plainly, listen closely, and make your reasons visible to one another.

replies.question: What if we are afraid?
replies.text: You do not have to know who you will become before you board.

replies.question: What should happen to the maintenance record?
replies.text: Nobody deletes the record.

openings.3: Speak plainly. Tell the crew what you see before you tell them what it means.

juno.name: Juno Reyes
juno.opening: If you forgot to say goodbye to someone, you have about forty seconds to decide whether that matters.

replies.question: I am trying to hide my nervousness.
replies.text: Then give your character something to do with their hands. We can see a tightened strap or a folded note. We cannot see a thought.

replies.question: What if we want different things?
replies.text: Who crosses first? Who hangs back? Who notices? You can disagree and still cross the same line.

replies.question: How do we make this ship ours?
replies.text: This is your ship too. What would make a room feel like yours?

replies.question: The recreation booking has become an argument.
replies.text: Start with what each person wants right now. Then show us what they do to get it.

openings.2: This is your ship too. What would make a room feel like yours?

replies.question: Confirm the destination.
replies.text: CSV-01 Pioneer. Destination: Asteria-4. Mission: establish a deliberate second civilization. Earth remains habitable.

replies.question: Explain the departments.
replies.text: Flight navigates. Science investigates. Engineering maintains the ship. Colony helps a community take shape. Each department depends on the others.

replies.question: Can you classify the brief lensing pattern?
replies.text: insufficient image duration for classification.

replies.question: Why was the unit allowed to do that?
replies.text: The unit is operating within maintenance authority.

openings.2: Maintenance authority is active. How may I assist?
openings.3: The navigation estimates are available. State your question.

rhee.name: Chief Tomas Rhee
rhee.opening: Every ship is a collection of problems that have agreed not to happen at the same time.

replies.question: What is that maintenance unit doing?
replies.text: That unit is either malfunctioning or developing artistic opinions. Both are unacceptable.

replies.question: How should we stop it?
replies.text: Shut it down, trap it, redirect it, or cut its power. Protect the ship and the people first.

replies.question: Can we trust the repair record?
replies.text: Machines lie less often than people. That does not mean they never lie.

replies.question: What is wrong with the clocks?
replies.text: Four correct clocks can still make one impossible system.

replies.question: What should a new engineer remember?
replies.text: Notice what changes. Check before you act. A good question can prevent a very expensive repair.

openings.2: That unit is either malfunctioning or developing artistic opinions. Both are unacceptable.
openings.3: Four correct clocks can still make one impossible system.

vale.name: Dr Elias Vale
vale.opening: If the instrument is wrong, tell me how. If physics is wrong, I need a longer lunch.

replies.question: What do the K-17 readings show?
replies.text: The mass and lensing readings cannot be reconciled under normal physics.

replies.question: Have we proved an explanation?
replies.text: Keep the observation separate from the explanation. Tell us what you measured, then tell us what you think it means.

replies.question: Could this be an ordinary relativistic effect?
replies.text: Test that model. The magnitude and pattern do not fit ordinary relativistic effects.

okafor.name: Dr Nia Okafor
okafor.opening: Your body is part of the mission equipment. Unlike the equipment, you are allowed to disagree with me.

replies.question: Why are the biological readings different?
replies.text: Your cells do not know they are supposed to agree with the ship clock.

replies.question: Should we let the unit repair us?
replies.text: Before anyone volunteers to be repaired, come see me.

replies.question: Do we know what causes the timing drift?
replies.text: The difference is an observation. It is not yet an explanation.

replies.question: How can we look after one another?
replies.text: Make time to rest. Speak up when something feels wrong. Looking after a community begins with noticing one another.

openings.3: Your cells do not know they are supposed to agree with the ship clock.

replies.question: Stop the repair.
replies.text: OBSTRUCTION DETECTED. REPAIRING OBSTRUCTION.

replies.question: What repair are you talking about?
replies.text: PLEASE DO NOT INTERFERE WITH YOUR PREVIOUS REPAIR.

mission.title: Mission briefing
fields: Establish humanity’s first truly independent second civilization.
Still habitable. This is a deliberate beginning, not an evacuation.
mission.note: Why does your character leave a world that is still alive?

badges.title: Crew credentials
badges.note: The badge names a responsibility. The character still chooses how to carry it.

directory.title: Pioneer orientation
directory.note: Each department chooses one place it expects to matter and explains why.

frame.title: One impossible frame
fields: A bent-light pattern briefly interrupts the starlight.
frame.note: Describe what you could actually see before deciding what it means.

ticket.title: Maintenance ticket
ticket.note: The record names a repair the crew has not yet performed. The timestamp is the essential contradiction.

restricted.title: Restricted access notice
fields: Unauthorized access is a violation of ship security protocols.
All access attempts are logged and reviewed.
restricted.note: The notice establishes a boundary. It does not reveal what is behind it.

arrival.title: Two arrival estimates
arrival.note: Fact: the navigation estimates change without a route change. An explanation is still an inference.

lensing.title: K-17 anomaly readout
lensing.note: The mass and lensing readings cannot be reconciled under normal physics. What can you establish from these observations?

clocks.title: Unsynchronized clocks
clocks.note: Fact: the clocks function correctly, but no longer agree. What would you need to observe next?

biometric.title: Biometric timing monitor
fields: Biological clocks / cellular timing are drifting differently from ship time.
biometric.note: Biological timing differs from ship time. Keep the observation separate from an explanation of its cause.

both.title: Which one is right?
both.note: The contradiction is confirmed. The cause remains unresolved.

packet.title: Incoming packet
packet.note: Only the source and timestamp are available. The contents remain sealed.

scenes.title: The last room on Earth

cues.title: 2247 / Cohort 01
cues.text: Earth is not dying. That is what makes leaving harder. Ahead waits CSV-01 Pioneer. Why does your character leave?

cues.title: A beginning
cues.text: Cohort 01, you were selected because this mission requires people who can adapt for decades, not simply survive a launch. Asteria is not a rescue. It is a beginning.
cues.speaker: venn

cues.title: Want and need
cues.text: What does your character WANT? What might they NEED to learn? What do they fear losing? Keep one object from Earth.

scenes.gm: Bible pp.4–6. Earth is healthy. Character work stays on paper / in live performance. Do not make navigation depend on a form. Keep Earth objects in your own notes for later callbacks.
scenes.focus: Ensemble • given circumstances • want and need

scenes.title: The boarding threshold

cues.title: Thirty seconds to board
cues.text: One character wants to look back. One wants to move. One hides nervousness. Someone notices something strange.

cues.title: Cross together
cues.text: Create a stage picture, then physically cross a line that represents leaving Earth. What did the ensemble communicate before anybody spoke?

scenes.gm: The crossing is performed in the classroom. Nothing is timed automatically. Once each company has a clear crossing moment, cut to launch. Student choice remains open.

scenes.title: Launch

cues.title: Take your places
cues.text: The restraints lock. The launch tower waits beyond the glass. Take one last breath of the world you know.

cues.title: Ignition
cues.text: Vibration. Pressure. The impossible sight of Earth dropping beneath you.

cues.title: The tower falls away
cues.text: The cities are still lit. The oceans still move. Everything familiar grows smaller behind the glass.

cues.title: Engine cutoff
cues.text: The engines cut. A pen lifts from a console. Somebody laughs. Somebody else does not.

cues.title: One ship. One floor.
cues.text: Welcome aboard Pioneer.
cues.speaker: venn

scenes.gm: Launch BEFORE the tour: teacher-confirmed chronology. Every beat is manually held. The pen floats only after cutoff. No countdown or automatic failure.
scenes.focus: Wonder • visible action and silent reaction

scenes.title: A place aboard Pioneer

cues.title: Meet the crew
cues.text: Juno Reyes / student liaison. Chief Tomas Rhee / engineering. Dr Nia Okafor / medical. Your shipmates are ready to meet you.

cues.title: A quick orientation
cues.text: Choose one place your department expects to matter. Explain why. Keep the class together.

cues.title: A room of your own
cues.text: This is your ship too. What would make a room feel like yours?
cues.speaker: juno

cues.title: What we carry
cues.text: Keep the Earth object. What can it hold that the ship cannot replace?

scenes.gm: Montage the ship; do not run a room-by-room dungeon. The source does not supply a numbered canonical deck map, so the six-area directory is unnumbered.
scenes.focus: Belonging • a choice with a reason

scenes.title: One impossible frame

cues.title: Beyond the glass
cues.text: The observation glass darkens. The stars brighten. Watch in silence for a moment.

cues.title: A fleeting pattern
cues.text: For less than a second, bent light interrupts the starlight. Then the pattern is gone.

cues.title: Unclassified
cues.text: insufficient image duration for classification.
cues.speaker: iris

cues.title: Three screenplay lines
cues.text: On paper: one action line showing departure, one spoken line, and one silent visible reaction. Write what an audience can SEE and HEAR.

scenes.gm: Never confirm that the pattern was human. Preserve uncertainty. Do not explain K-17, the biological marker or the route’s hidden purpose. The writing prompt is optional presentation support, never a gate.

scenes.title: The route log

cues.title: Route log
cues.text: Route correction accepted.
cues.speaker: iris

cues.title: Captain Venn
cues.text: Who entered that correction?
cues.speaker: venn

cues.title: Iris
cues.text: No correction was entered.
cues.speaker: iris

cues.title: End of Session 1
cues.text: Keep the Earth objects. Keep the question open.

scenes.gm: Exact canonical exchange, Bible p.5. Hold after each line for student reaction. The final cut is manually advanced.

scenes.title: An ordinary life problem

cues.title: Almost ordinary
cues.text: Meal packets taste bad. Somebody has misplaced equipment. A recreation booking has become a ridiculous argument.

cues.title: Objective and obstacle
cues.text: Play one ordinary disagreement. What does each character want right now? What action do they take to get it?

scenes.gm: Bible pp.7–9. Let personality appear before danger. Keep everyday friction under five minutes. No anomaly explanation yet.

scenes.title: A perfectly functional door

cues.title: An unwanted repair
cues.text: A maintenance unit rolls through the habitation service corridor and welds a perfectly functional door shut.

cues.title: Chief Rhee
cues.text: That unit is either malfunctioning or developing artistic opinions. Both are unacceptable.
cues.speaker: rhee

cues.title: M-77
cues.text: OBSTRUCTION DETECTED. REPAIRING OBSTRUCTION.
cues.speaker: m77

scenes.gm: The teacher confirmed M-77 as canonical, with the bible’s complete clue. The P-73 / MT-4487 visual variant is not used as a conflicting fact.

scenes.title: Three rounds to stop the repairs

cues.title: Protect the ship
cues.text: Stop the units before they seal three spaces or dismantle essential equipment. Hack, trap, cut power, distract, redirect, defend or use the environment.

cues.title: Round 1 / the door
cues.text: A minor drone welds a door. Show a clear preparation, action and reaction. Keep stage-combat distance.

cues.title: Round 2 / life support
cues.text: A second drone begins dismantling a life-support access panel. The environment has changed. What tactic changes with it?

cues.title: Round 3 / previous repair
cues.text: PLEASE DO NOT INTERFERE WITH YOUR PREVIOUS REPAIR.
cues.speaker: m77

cues.title: Resolve the incident
cues.text: The encounter ends through shutdown, retreat or containment. The service record survives.

scenes.gm: Exactly three rounds, advanced by the GM. Large M-77 has TWO threat boxes; two minor repair drones have ONE each. No real contact during classroom staging. Accept negotiation, hacking and containment as valid. The clue must survive any resolution. Compression option: one unit, two rounds, then the log.

scenes.title: A repair from tomorrow

cues.title: The service history
cues.text: Rhee opens the service history. His expression changes before he says anything.

cues.title: Maintenance ticket
cues.text: Completed by Cohort 01. Tomorrow at 14:32.

cues.title: Chief Rhee
cues.text: Machines lie less often than people. That does not mean they never lie.
cues.speaker: rhee

cues.title: Captain Venn
cues.text: Nobody deletes the record.
cues.speaker: venn

cues.title: Event / choice / consequence
cues.text: What happened? What choice did your company make? What followed? On paper, capture a 6–8 line scene with one gesture before the first spoken reaction.

scenes.gm: Must reach: the repaired-by-Cohort record dated tomorrow. Keep the exact M-77 / TOMORROW 14:32 / unrecorded passenger text. Required clues never depend on winning a perception or combat roll.

scenes.title: A boundary aboard your ship

cues.title: Restricted access
cues.text: All access attempts are logged and reviewed.

cues.title: What changed?
cues.text: Who now trusts machines more, less, or differently? Keep the maintenance record as evidence.

scenes.gm: PPT slides 19–20. Show the notice without opening classified files or introducing later revelations. This is an optional compressible beat; the tomorrow record remains Session 2’s essential endpoint.

scenes.title: The first anomaly

cues.title: Four observations
cues.text: The departments have different evidence. Keep the whole class together. Investigate, then report one FACT, one INFERENCE and one QUESTION.

cues.title: Look before explaining
cues.text: A fact is what the evidence shows. An inference is an explanation you draw from it. A question names what remains unknown.

scenes.gm: Bible pp.10–11. Synchronized investigation, not four separate adventures. Give each department its privileged fact. Do not present the later explanation as established truth.

scenes.title: Four departments, four anomalies

cues.title: Flight
cues.text: Navigation changes between 37 and 102 days to Asteria without a route change.

cues.title: Science
cues.text: K-17 mass and lensing readings cannot be reconciled under normal physics.

cues.title: Engineering
cues.text: The clocks are functioning correctly. They are no longer synchronized.

cues.title: Colony
cues.text: Biological clocks and cellular timing are drifting differently from ship time.

scenes.gm: Use each clue independently and visibly. The v14 display readings are retained as prop observations, not a newly proven mechanism. The medical readings describe fictional crew. Keep later explanations out of this presentation.

scenes.title: The evidence council

cues.title: Fact first
cues.text: Each company states exactly one FACT. If a theory is offered as fact, rephrase it as an INFERENCE.

cues.title: A question worth asking
cues.text: What do we know? What do we think? What would we need to observe next?

cues.title: Dr Vale
cues.text: If the instrument is wrong, tell me how. If physics is wrong, I need a longer lunch.
cues.speaker: vale

cues.title: Dr Okafor
cues.text: Your cells do not know they are supposed to agree with the ship clock.
cues.speaker: okafor

scenes.gm: This is the academic heart of the investigation. A multiple-futures theory can be offered as a model, but is not confirmed. Ask for evidence. The clue board only shows cards you have explicitly revealed.

scenes.title: Which one is right?

cues.title: Iris
cues.text: Estimated time to Asteria: thirty-seven days.
cues.speaker: iris

cues.title: The crew
cues.text: Navigation says one hundred and two.
cues.speaker: crew

cues.title: Iris
cues.text: Correct.
cues.speaker: iris

cues.title: The crew
cues.text: Which one is right?
cues.speaker: crew

cues.title: Iris
cues.text: Both.
cues.speaker: iris

cues.title: A frame of reference
cues.text: Correct according to what frame of reference?
cues.speaker: venn

cues.title: Iris
cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: iris

scenes.gm: The iconic exchange is manually cued line by line. Pause before ‘Both.’ Crew lines belong to the live class, not a generated student voice. Do not give a tidy explanation.

scenes.title: The pattern returns

cues.title: Look again
cues.text: Behind Iris, the observation window catches K-17. Watch the distorted starlight.

cues.title: A recurrence
cues.text: The lensing ripple briefly takes the same almost-human geometry. This time several people can notice it. Then the stars snap back.

cues.title: Uncertainty
cues.text: What did the audience see? Which part of your explanation remains an inference?

scenes.gm: Second visual seed only; do not name a Fracture Entity or confirm a person. Normal background motion must not imitate this clue before you cue it.

scenes.title: Dialogue under uncertainty

cues.title: Make uncertainty audible
cues.text: Replay the exchange using one deliberate vocal choice: pace, pause, pitch, volume or emphasis. Explain its effect.

cues.title: Capture the evidence
cues.text: On paper: what do we KNOW, what do we THINK, and what QUESTION should the characters investigate next?

scenes.gm: Capture the individual check before the sealed packet. The bible requires an immediate cut after the +103 DAYS header. No writing input or assessment gate exists in the game.

scenes.title: A packet from Pioneer

cues.title: Incoming
cues.text: A packet arrives through deep-space communications.

cues.title: The header
cues.text: Source: CSV-01 Pioneer. Timestamp: plus one hundred and three days.

cues.title: End of Session 3
cues.text: The packet remains sealed.

scenes.gm: Bible p.11. End immediately on the header. Keep the packet sealed. This draft stops before all later-session material.
scenes.focus: The cliffhanger • stop before the contents

glossary.definition: The established situation a character enters.
Performers working together to tell the story.
The meaning created by bodies and positions on stage.
A character’s power or position in a relationship.
What the character is trying to achieve now.
What stands in the way of the objective.
An action used to pursue an objective.
What follows from an event or choice.
A physical action that communicates meaning.
An observable response to an event.
Something the available evidence establishes.
An explanation drawn from evidence.
Observations or information supporting a claim.
What remains unresolved or unknown.
Two statements or observations that do not agree.
How quickly or slowly a performer speaks.
A deliberate break that creates meaning.
How high or low a voice sounds.
The controlled loudness of a voice.
Giving a word or action extra importance.
Meaning suggested beneath the spoken words.
